subject: Patrick Clerkin City Council Candidacy
overview: The Medford Bytes podcast interviewed City Council candidate Patrick Clerkin regarding his 2025 platform and prior political experience. The discussion focused on local communications infrastructure, the jurisdictional boundaries of municipal government, and his involvement in national political movements.

items.title: Introduction and Candidate Background
items.summary: Patrick Clerkin introduced himself as a mechanical engineer and nine-year Medford resident running for City Council to build on his 2023 campaign experience.

items.title: Medford Community Network Project
items.summary: Clerkin described his work developing a local social media and information hub designed to centralize Medford-specific media and provide a moderated alternative to anonymous forums.

items.title: National Politics and Health Industry Critique
items.summary: The candidate detailed his involvement with the RFK Jr. presidential campaign and a unity coalition, citing concerns about industrial chemicals, the pharmaceutical lobby, and the food supply.

items.title: Public Health and Policy Discussion
items.summary: Clerkin responded to host pushback regarding vaccine skepticism and clarified his views on pharmaceutical industry oversight and bioweapons research.

items.title: Jurisdiction of Local Government
items.summary: The discussion centered on whether the City Council should address global issues like the Gaza ceasefire, with Clerkin arguing that such topics distract from core municipal functions while the host advocated for their importance to constituents.

items.title: Campaign Outreach and Closing
items.summary: Clerkin provided his campaign website and announced he would hold weekly in-person office hours at Colleen's leading up to the election.
